atoms.text: 60 children from Roundhill School were asked what type of transport they normally use to get to school. Their answers are shown in this pie chart.

instruction.text: Use the pie chart to decide if the statement is true or false.

atoms.a: The number of children that walk to school is 30.

wrong.text: The pie chart shows that half of the children walk to school, and half of 60 is 30.

atoms.a: Half of the children take the bus to school.

wrong.text: The sector that represents taking the bus is much smaller than half of the pie chart.

atoms.a: A quarter of the children ride their bikes to school.

wrong.text: The sector that represents cycling to school is a quarter of the pie chart.

atoms.a: The most popular option is walking to school.

wrong.text: The largest sector of the pie chart is the one that represents walking to school.

atoms.a: 20 children take the bus to school.

wrong.text: 20 is a third of 60, but the sector that represents taking the bus to school doesn’t take up a third of the pie chart.

atoms.a: The least popular option is getting to school by car.

wrong.text: The smallest sector on the pie chart is the one that represents taking the bus to school, so that is the least popular option.

atoms.a: None of the children take the train to school.

wrong.text: There is no sector that represents taking the train to school, so nobody chose that option.

instruction.text: Use the pie chart to fill in the gaps in the table.
